findings.title: 60 of 62 records self-certify support with no reviewer verdict and no artifact hash
findings.evidence: Every record carries acceptance_authority='astra-lead-literature (ledger author; author self-assessment, not a reviewer verdict)' and review_status='not_independently_reviewed' (62/62). 60/62 records additionally set author_asserts_supports=true (only T-105 and T-513 do not); 50 of those also set content_status='verified'. No record schema contains artifact_refs/artifact_sha256. This is the HF-14 detector pattern at ledger-record level: supports_claim=true with no independent reviewer verdict field and no artifact hash.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add an independent-reviewer verdict field per record and bind each verified record to a reviewer + artifact hash, or (b) rename content_status/author_asserts_supports so the field cannot read as acceptance (e.g. source_read_status) and require the L0 acceptance to be carried by a separate reviewer-verdict artifact. Do not let the author's own assessment satisfy G-LIT.

findings.title: 8 records disjoin two frozen class ids in one record
findings.evidence: evaluation_rubric.yaml:52-54: 'Exactly these class IDs may appear... Classes are not interchangeable and must never be disjoined in a statement.' D-004 (line 4) carries ['AF-SCC-C2-VAC-GEN','AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN']; T-303 (line 25) and T-526 (line 58) each carry C0 and C2 plus a theorem conclusion; T-305 (line 27), T-402 (line 30), T-515 (line 46), T-528 (line 60), D-005 (line 5) likewise. The project's class-separation detector does not scan ledger rows, so it reports the ledger clean.
findings.recommendation: Split each multi-class record into one record per class (or a record-class table), and extend class_separation.py to scan ledger/theorems.jsonl class_ids for cardinality > 1.

findings.title: 3 C0-bound records are typed `theorem`, which evaluation_rubric.yaml forbids for this class
findings.evidence: evaluation_rubric.yaml:100-104 (frozen_classes AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN status_risk): known C0-extendibility results are an open-set counterexample candidate for the class as literally stated, and 'this class' status MUST be recorded as conditional or refuted_candidate, never open_conjecture and never theorem'. T-302 (line 24, Sbierski 2018 C0-inextendibility of maximal analytic Schwarzschild), T-303 (line 25, Luk 2018 weak null singularities with C0 extension), T-526 (line 58) are all typed conclusion_type=theorem on that class. T-303 in particular records an extendibility result, i.e. evidence against generic C0, yet is bound to the C0 class with content_status=verified.
findings.recommendation: Re-type C0 records to conditional_theorem/refuted_candidate with an explicit transfer or scope note, or move non-generic single-spacetime results out of the generic class.

findings.title: 15 quantity-bearing statements carry no quantity_check; the field does not exist in the ledger schema
findings.evidence: G-LIT criterion 4 and the literature verifier require a quantity_check for rates/exponents/codimensions/counts; HF-04 is the detector. A deterministic regex over statement_exact found 15 records with quantity tokens (codimension, exponent, O(...), dimensional, rate, measure/fraction phrasing) and no quantity_check field; the ledger schema (24 fields) has no such field on any record, so the check can never pass.
findings.recommendation: Add a quantity_check field (value, source locator, tolerance) to the record schema and populate it for the 15 rows, or strip the quantities from the statement_exact into a clearly labelled 'as quoted' field with the check attached.

findings.title: 0 of 97 sources record matter/Lambda/dimension/symmetry/formulation scope as fields
findings.evidence: G-LIT criterion 3 and the literature verifier require the source's matter model, cosmological constant, dimension, symmetry and formulation to be explicitly recorded per source. The L1 registry schema has no such fields (registry keys: arxiv_id, authors, bibkey, doi, notes, reviewer, source_id, status, title, url, venue, verification, year). Scope is only inferable from free-text notes. The frozen_classes forbidden_evidence rules are therefore not machine-checkable against the evidence metadata.
findings.recommendation: Add the five scope fields to the registry row schema and populate them; then the class forbidden_evidence check can actually run on L0 rows.

findings.title: citation_support == 1.0 is not computable: 78 of 97 sources use status `verified-api`, which has no rubric weight
findings.evidence: metrics.citation_support (evaluation_rubric.yaml:260-263) defines weights only for verified_primary / verified_secondary / partial / unresolved / contradicted. The registry uses status values verified-primary (19) and verified-api (78). No mapping exists for verified-api, so the G-LIT criterion 'every claim's evidence set has citation_support == 1.0' cannot be evaluated, and MANIFEST's aggregate counts.verified_sources=97 is unsupported by the rubric vocabulary.
findings.recommendation: Define the weight of verified-api (e.g. secondary=0.5 or a distinct api_metadata=0.25) in evaluation_rubric.yaml, or rename the registry statuses to the rubric vocabulary and recompute per-row citation_support.

findings.title: artifacts/literature/L0_L1_ACCEPTANCE.md declares 'L0 gaps: none' and 'L1 gaps: none' while B1-B6 hold
findings.evidence: L0_L1_ACCEPTANCE.md#fde5600b45a5 states '- L0 gaps' / '- none' and '- L1 gaps' / '- none'. Measured at the same revision: 8 disjunctive records (B2), 3 C0 theorem records (B3), 60 self-certified records (B1), 15 unchecked quantities (B4), 78 unweighted source statuses (B6), 5 unassessed sources.
findings.recommendation: Replace the 'none' gap statements with the measured defect list (or gate the file on the checker exiting zero); an acceptance document that contradicts its own artifact is itself a G-AUDIT finding.

findings.title: 21 records carry neither class_ids nor informs_classes
findings.evidence: Records D-006, T-104, T-207, T-502..T-504, T-507..T-509, T-512..T-514, T-517..T-522, D-008, D-009, T-529 carry empty class_ids and no informs_classes, so G-LIT criterion 3 ('statement scope matched to class_id') has no referent for them. Several are formal/methodological entries that may legitimately be class-free; the ledger should say so explicitly rather than leave the field empty.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit class_scope='none (methodological)' marker, or fill in informs_classes.

findings.title: 5 unassessed sources and 11 accepted rows with metadata-only anchors
findings.evidence: MANIFEST counts.unassessed_sources = [SRC-090, SRC-092, SRC-093, SRC-096, SRC-097]; metadata_only_sources = 12; accepted_with_metadata_anchors lists 11 record ids (D-001, T-105, T-208, T-501, T-506, T-511, T-514, T-517, T-518, T-520, T-521). None of those rows' evidence sets can reach citation_support 1.0 while an anchor is metadata-only. The rows do carry honest caveats (e.g. T-513 is correctly rejected), so this is a scope-honesty backlog item, not a silent failure.
findings.recommendation: Keep them provisional until an abstract or full text is read; do not count them toward citation_support=1.0.

findings.title: unresolved.jsonl aggregates only 12 of the 62 rows' unresolved items
findings.evidence: All 62 ledger records carry a non-empty unresolved[] list (row-level criterion satisfied); the aggregate artifacts/literature/unresolved.jsonl has 12 distinct theorem_ids. The aggregate is therefore not a complete view, and its rows use status='provisional' rather than an open/closed vocabulary.
findings.recommendation: Generate unresolved.jsonl mechanically from the ledger's unresolved[] fields so the aggregate cannot drift from the rows.

findings.title: 30 theorem-typed records have no artifact_refs/hash; claim-scope applicability is genuinely contested and not resolved here
findings.evidence: HF-01's detector is written for claim.conclusion_type == theorem with no artifact_refs; 30 ledger records are typed theorem and the ledger schema has no artifact_refs field for any record. The ledger author's reading (recorded in reviews/L0-review-093.json) is that HF-01 is claim-scoped. I do not silently resolve that; I record that the detector fires literally on 30 records and that B1 (HF-14) already blocks acceptance regardless.
findings.recommendation: Gate adjudication: decide explicitly whether ledger records are claims for HF-01 purposes; if yes, re-type or bind them.

findings.title: Field-vocabulary drift: status vs resolution_status; content_status=verified vs verification_status=abstract-read
findings.evidence: G-LIT criterion 1 asks for resolution_status; the registry field is status. Records say content_status='verified' while verification_status='abstract-read' (61/62) or 'unverified' (1/62); a reader can read 'verified' as theorem-verified when the row means 'source metadata/abstract read'. The vocabulary is defined nowhere in the ledger itself.
findings.recommendation: Publish the field vocabulary in the ledger's schema/manifest and align it with evaluation_rubric.yaml.
